text: Write the standard `equals` skeleton, in the order the checks should appear. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: Point(int x, int y) { this.x = x; this.y = y; }
if (___) return true;               // fast path: same object
if (!(___)) return false;           // type check and bind in one step
@Override public int hashCode() { return java.util.Objects.hash(x, y); }
answer: this == o|o instanceof Point p|p.x == x && p.y == y
explanation: Verified: true. The identity check is an optimisation and the `instanceof` pattern handles the null case for free — `null instanceof Point` is false, so no separate null test is needed. Note the parameter is `Object`: writing `equals(Point o)` is an overload rather than an override, the collections keep calling the inherited version, and only `@Override` catches it.
